intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the heart of Marrakech at the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Arrive mid-morning to explore the labyrinthine souks of the Medina, visit the Medersa Ben Youssef Islamic school, and end at the square as it transforms into a vibrant open-air theatre by evening with storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Staying in a nearby riad ensures you can walk directly to the action without wasting transit time, especially important given a late Day 1 arrival.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Discover Marrakech's royal history with a self-guided or local-guide tour of the 19th-century Bahia Palace and the ornate 16th-century Saadian Tombs. Both sites are within walking distance of each other in the southern Medina, making this a highly efficient half-day itinerary. Booking a local guide through your riad the evening before maximises morning hours and avoids midday heat. Ideal for Days 2 or 3 when you are fully settled.

experiences.name: Atlas Mountains Day Trek & Berber Village Visit
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided trek into the foothills of the High Atlas Mountains, visiting the traditional Berber village of Imlil. Hike scenic trails, share mint tea with a local family, and gain insight into centuries-old Amazigh culture. Operators depart from central Marrakech by 08:00, returning by 18:00, making it a perfect full-day adventure on Days 3 or 4. Choose operators based near Gueliz or the Medina to cut pickup time.
experiences.location: Imlil Village, High Atlas Mountains, 60km from Marrakech

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp at Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Travel to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for the centrepiece desert experience. Ride camels at sunset into the dunes, dine on traditional tagine under the stars, and sleep in a comfortable Berber camp. Wake before dawn for a sunrise over the Sahara. To maximise time, take an overnight bus or shared transfer from Marrakech on Day 4 evening, spend Days 5–6 in the desert, and return Day 7. This keeps the experience within budget when booked as a package.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Marrakech Street Food & Cooking Class in the Medina
experiences.description: Start with a guided street food walk through the Medina's spice souks and food stalls, sampling harira soup, msemen flatbread, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Transition into a hands-on Moroccan cooking class hosted in a traditional riad kitchen, learning to prepare a lamb tagine and bastilla pastry. Schedule this on Day 2 afternoon so it doubles as cultural orientation after your late Day 1 arrival. Many riad-based classes are a short walk from accommodation in the Medina.
experiences.location: Mouassine & Rahba Kedima Souk Area, Medina, Marrakech

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Settle in after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget petit taxi (~30–40 MAD) from the airport to Marrakech Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, then take a gentle introductory stroll through the southern edge of the Medina. Walk along Rue Riad Zitoun el Kedim toward Jemaa el-Fna square to get your bearings. Peek into the square and soak up the atmosphere — snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians are already active by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your first evening fully immersed in Jemaa el-Fna square as the food stalls fire up at sunset. Browse the open-air food court — a true Marrakech ritual. Watch acrobats and musicians perform under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Eaten on the plane or grab a quick café au lait and msemen (Moroccan flatbread) at a local café near the hotel for ~15 MAD.
meals.lunch: Grab a street snack near the airport or in the Medina on arrival — a harira soup bowl and bread at a local stall costs ~20 MAD.
meals.dinner: Eat at the Jemaa el-Fna food stalls (stalls #1–32) — a full meal of brochettes, salad, bread, and fresh orange juice costs ~60–80 MAD per person. Authentic and unbeatable value.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00 — allow 45–60 minutes for baggage and customs. Petit taxis are metered; insist on the meter or agree on a fare beforehand. Exchange some cash at the airport (bureau de change) for MAD. The Medina is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior — non-Muslims cannot enter) for a peaceful start and iconic photos. Then walk 10 minutes to the Saadian Tombs, a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis. Entry fee: ~70 MAD. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Bahia Palace (~70 MAD entry), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with ornate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) nearby — visit the Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation) and wander the spice-scented souks of the southern Medina.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna for sunset, then climb to a rooftop café terrace (Café de France or Café Glacier) for a mint tea (~15 MAD) with panoramic views of the square. Explore the northern souks by night — the lantern-lit alleyways are magical after dark.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a local café — café au lait, amlou (almond-argan spread), and khobz bread for ~25–35 MAD.
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant near Bahia Palace — a tagine or couscous set lunch costs ~50–70 MAD. Try Restaurant Chez Bahia on Rue Riad Zitoun el Jdid.
meals.dinner: Street food around Jemaa el-Fna — merguez sandwiches, fried fish, or a bowl of snail soup (babouche) for ~30–50 MAD total.

day_by_day.notes: Combine the Saadian Tombs and Bahia Palace visits — they are a 5-minute walk apart. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) out of respect.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (~70 MAD entry), the finest example of Marinid Islamic architecture in Marrakech. Intricate stucco, zellige tilework, and a serene courtyard await. Nearby, explore the Marrakech Museum (housed in Dar Menebhi Palace, ~50 MAD) for Moroccan art and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive deep into the souks — navigate the labyrinthine alleys of the northern Medina. Visit the Souk des Teinturiers (Dyers' Souk) to see vibrant wool being dyed in open vats, and the Souk Smarine for textiles and crafts. Browse but budget for a small souvenir (leather goods, argan oil, ceramics).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Mouassine neighborhood for a quieter, more local evening. Visit the Mouassine Fountain and explore artisan workshops. Have dinner in this trendy but authentic quarter.

meals.breakfast: Msemen with honey and argan oil at a Medina café near Ben Youssef — ~20 MAD.
meals.lunch: Snack lunch in the souks — a fresh-squeezed orange juice (~4 MAD), a kefta sandwich (~20 MAD), and dried fruit from a stall (~10 MAD).
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Mouassine quarter — try a chicken bastilla or lamb tagine for ~60–80 MAD. Ask locals for their favorite spot to avoid tourist-trap pricing.

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa is a highlight — budget at least 45 minutes inside. The souks can be disorienting; embrace getting lost but keep Google Maps offline downloaded as a backup. Avoid guides who approach you unsolicited — they expect large tips.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (06:00–07:00) on a shared desert tour bus or budget CTM/Supratours bus toward Ouarzazate and the Sahara Desert (Merzouga). A shared budget group tour (2-day/1-night Sahara trip) costs approximately 400–600 MAD per person all-inclusive — book in advance from Marrakech guesthouses or agencies like Sahara Desert Tours. The route passes through the stunning Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Aït Benhaddou (~30 minutes from Ouarzazate) — a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) and famous film location (Game of Thrones, Gladiator). Explore the ancient earthen citadel on foot (~10 MAD entry or negotiate with guide). Continue driving through the Draa Valley — date palms, kasbahs, and ochre landscapes unfold.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Sahara (Merzouga or Zagora depending on tour). Mount camels at sunset for a 1-hour ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes — one of the most spectacular experiences in Morocco. Arrive at a budget desert camp as the stars emerge.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure — bread, jam, and coffee (~20–25 MAD) or included in tour package.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside Berber café near Ouarzazate — harira, bread, and tea for ~40–50 MAD.
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp package — traditional Berber dinner around a campfire (tagine, couscous, mint tea) under a sky full of stars.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sahara tour 1–2 days in advance from Marrakech. Shared group tours (8–12 people) are the most budget-friendly option. Bring a warm layer — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. A headscarf or buff is useful against sand. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 06:00) to climb the nearest sand dune and watch the Sahara sunrise — a once-in-a-lifetime experience. The golden light on the dunes is extraordinary. Take a morning camel ride back to the camp or the road. After breakfast at camp, begin the return journey toward Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Skoura Oasis — a lush palm grove with ancient kasbahs, perfect for a short walk. Continue through the Valley of Roses (Kelaat M'Gouna region) — in mid-March, early rose blooms may be visible. Visit a roadside argan cooperative where women press argan oil — usually free to visit with no obligation to buy.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (18:00–19:00). Rest, shower, and recover at the hotel. Take a quiet evening walk in the Medina or relax at a hammam.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp — Berber bread, olive oil, honey, eggs, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop on the return journey — a simple tagine at a local restaurant for ~50–60 MAD.
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech — treat yourself to a sit-down restaurant dinner. Try Earth Café (vegetarian, ~80–100 MAD) or a local Medina eatery for a well-earned proper meal.

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long (5–7 hours with stops). Bring snacks and water for the bus. March weather in the Sahara is ideal — warm days (~25°C) and cool nights. If you have extra energy on return, the hammam experience (public hammam ~15–20 MAD, or a tourist hammam ~100–150 MAD) is perfect for sore muscles after camel riding.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (~70 MAD entry, or ~140 MAD including the Berber Museum inside) — a stunning botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent. The cobalt blue buildings and exotic plants are iconic. Arrive at opening time (08:00) to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gueliz neighborhood (Ville Nouvelle / New Town) — a contrast to the Medina with wide boulevards, galleries, and modern Moroccan life. Visit the Yves Saint Laurent Museum if budget allows (~80 MAD) or browse the Marché Central for local produce and affordable souvenirs. Walk along Avenue Mohammed V.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina for a final evening of souvenir shopping in the souks. Bargain for leather goods, lanterns, spices, or argan products. End the evening at Jemaa el-Fna one last time — enjoy the spectacle of the square in full festive mode on a Saturday night.

meals.breakfast: Café Kif Kif or any Gueliz café near Majorelle — café au lait and croissant for ~30–40 MAD.
meals.lunch: Marché Central area — a fresh sandwich or pastilla from a local bakery for ~25–35 MAD.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for your last full dinner — try Restaurant Al Fassia (moderate pricing, ~120–150 MAD) for authentic Moroccan cuisine, or keep it budget with a final Jemaa el-Fna food stall feast (~60–80 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden gets very crowded by mid-morning on weekends — arrive at opening. The Gueliz neighborhood is a great place to buy fixed-price souvenirs without bargaining stress. Saturday night at Jemaa el-Fna is particularly lively — musicians, dancers, and storytellers are out in full force.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD entry), a vast 16th-century palace now largely in ruins but hauntingly beautiful. Storks nest on the battlements in spring. Climb the ramparts for views over the Medina. Nearby, browse the Mellah market (Jewish Quarter market) for local produce and a slice of authentic Marrakchi daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: if afternoon/evening flight, pack up, check out of the hotel, and store luggage at reception. Take a final mint tea on a rooftop terrace. Head to the airport via petit taxi (~30–40 MAD) allowing 2 hours before departure. If the flight is the next day, use this afternoon for any missed sights or last-minute shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of culture, desert, history, and adventure across one of the world's most captivating destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a Medina café — amlou, msemen, hard-boiled eggs, olives, and mint tea (~25–35 MAD). Savor every bite!
meals.lunch: Light lunch near El Badi Palace — a sandwich or bowl of harira soup from a street stall (~25–30 MAD).
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or grab a final snack at the Medina before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.notes: El Badi Palace is one of Marrakech's most underrated sights — far fewer tourists than Bahia Palace. Check flight time carefully and plan taxi departure accordingly (Marrakech airport is only 15–20 minutes from the Medina). Keep some MAD for the taxi and any last purchases, but exchange remaining dirhams before departure as MAD is a restricted currency hard to exchange abroad. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights): 2,500–3,500 MAD (~$250–$350 USD) per person, covering accommodation, transport, entry fees, meals, and the Sahara tour.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Marrakech Boutique Stay in the Medina area (~30 min). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your riad.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Jemaa el-Fna square to absorb the atmosphere — snake charmers, storytellers, and market stalls. Stroll into the northern edge of the souks to get your bearings without pressure to buy. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior) for a classic first Marrakech photo.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset transform Jemaa el-Fna into a massive open-air food theatre. Explore the food stalls for a casual first dinner experience. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Snack on the plane or grab a mint tea and msemen (Moroccan flatbread) at a café near the riad upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light meal at a rooftop café overlooking Jemaa el-Fna — try harira soup and a kefta sandwich (budget ~100–150 MAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Jemaa el-Fna night market food stalls — grilled merguez, snail soup, and fresh orange juice. Authentic and affordable (~80–120 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange currency at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina. Avoid aggressive touts by being politely firm.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning exploring the Marrakech Medina's historic core. Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (9th-century Islamic college, stunning Moorish architecture). Then explore the nearby Marrakech Museum housed in the Dar Menebhi Palace. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive deep into the souks — navigate the Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk with vivid wool), and the Souk Cherratine (leather). Visit the Bahia Palace (14th-century, ornate rooms and gardens). End with a wander through the mellah (Jewish quarter) and its covered market.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or hammam experience. Book a traditional hammam at a mid-range local hammam (not a tourist spa) for a genuine scrub and steam session (~150–250 MAD). Afterward, enjoy a quiet dinner near the riad.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the riad — most boutique riads include Moroccan breakfast with mint tea, amlou (almond-argan dip), bread, and eggs.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices in the Rahba Kedima spice square — tagine or pastilla (~120–180 MAD). Great people-watching terrace.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Jardin restaurant in the Mouassine neighbourhood — Moroccan cuisine in a beautiful garden courtyard (~200–280 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Madrasa and Marrakech Museum offer a combined ticket (~70 MAD). Wear comfortable shoes — souk cobblestones are uneven. Bargaining in souks is expected; start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley in the Atlas Mountains (45 min from Marrakech). Hire a shared grand taxi or join a small group tour (~200–300 MAD). Walk along the Ourika River, visit a traditional Berber village, and see local women's cooperative making argan products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the valley to the Setti Fatma waterfalls — a moderate 45-minute hike to the first cascade with rewarding views. Cool your feet in the mountain stream. Return to Marrakech by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum area (Gueliz neighbourhood, modern Marrakech). The garden closes at 18:00 but the surrounding area is pleasant for an evening stroll. Explore the Gueliz district for a change of pace from the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Riverside Berber restaurant in Ourika Valley — fresh trout from the river, Berber tagine, and mint tea with mountain views (~100–150 MAD). Several simple but charming options line the valley road.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gueliz at Kechmara — a popular Franco-Moroccan bistro with a relaxed vibe, great cocktails (mocktails available), and solid food (~180–250 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers — Atlas Mountain mornings can be cool in March. The Ourika Valley is best visited on a non-market day (Monday is market day and gets very crowded). Bring cash as ATMs are scarce outside Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via the Dades Valley — a full-day scenic drive (~9–10 hours total, usually done with a private driver or small group tour). Cross the High Atlas via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation, stunning mountain scenery). Stop at Aït Benhaddou — the UNESCO-listed ksar (fortified village) used in Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley — endless palmeries, kasbahs, and rose-growing villages. Stop in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') briefly. Pass through the Dades Gorge or Todra Gorge area depending on route. Arrive at your desert camp/hotel near Merzouga or Zagora by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 1-hour camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes (Merzouga). Watch the Sahara sunset paint the dunes orange and red. Overnight at a mid-range desert camp with private tent, dinner, and Berber music around the campfire under a spectacular starry sky.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure.
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch in Aït Benhaddou or Ouarzazate — a local restaurant serving tagine and Berber bread (~100–150 MAD). Your driver will recommend reliable spots.
meals.dinner: Dinner included at the desert camp — traditional Moroccan feast (harira, tagine, couscous, pastilla) eaten by candlelight in the camp tent. Berber musicians play after dinner (~included in camp package, typically 600–1000 MAD/night for mid-range).

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable mid-range desert camp in advance — look for camps with private tents and proper bathrooms. March weather in the Sahara is ideal: warm days (~25°C) and cool nights (~10°C). Bring a warm layer for the evening. The drive is long but the scenery is extraordinary — this is one of Morocco's great road journeys.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (5:30 AM) to watch the Sahara sunrise from the dunes — an unmissable experience. Return to camp for a Moroccan breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a longer morning camel trek. Explore the edge of the erg on foot and visit the nearby village of Merzouga to see the local nomadic lifestyle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via an alternative southern route through the Draa Valley and Agdz. Stop at the Tamnougalt Kasbah — one of Morocco's oldest fortified villages. Drive through endless date palm oases along the Draa River. Alternatively, if time allows, stop at the rose valley near El Kelaa M'Gouna (famous for rose harvest in May, but beautiful year-round).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in a mid-point town (Ouarzazate or Dades) for an overnight stop, OR push back to Marrakech if energy allows (arrive ~21:00). Recommend breaking the journey in Ouarzazate for a more relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp — Moroccan bread, honey, argan oil, mint tea, and eggs.
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch at a local restaurant in Agdz or Zagora — mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) or tagine (~100–150 MAD).
meals.dinner: If staying in Ouarzazate: dinner at Chez Dimitri (a historic restaurant, open since 1928, loved by film crews) — mixed Moroccan and international menu (~180–250 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: The return route via the Draa Valley is different from the outbound Tizi n'Tichka route, giving you two completely different landscapes. If returning directly to Marrakech, depart Merzouga by 10:00 AM. Confirm your driver's plan the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Marrakech (if overnighted en route, ~4-hour drive). Check back into your riad. After settling in, visit the Saadian Tombs — the lavishly decorated 16th-century royal mausoleum rediscovered in 1917. Nearby, explore the El Badi Palace ruins — a once-magnificent 16th-century palace, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mellah (Jewish quarter) and its historic synagogues. Then head to the Musée de la Photographie de Marrakech for a fascinating visual history of Morocco. Spend the late afternoon at leisure — browse the souks for last-minute gifts or simply sit in a café with mint tea.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a memorable farewell-to-Marrakech dinner at a traditional Moroccan riad restaurant. Enjoy a full multi-course Moroccan feast with live Gnaoua music. Return to the riad for a final night.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at en-route café or riad upon return.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad restaurant (rooftop, modern Moroccan cuisine, great views over the spice market) — (~180–220 MAD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout or a similar upscale-but-authentic riad restaurant — full Moroccan banquet experience with pastilla, tagine, couscous, and dessert (~350–500 MAD per person, a worthwhile splurge for the final night).

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs require tickets (~70 MAD) and can get crowded — arrive at opening (9:00 AM) or after 15:00. El Badi Palace is adjacent and worth the additional ticket (~10 MAD). Book the dinner restaurant in advance as popular riad restaurants fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Depending on your flight time, enjoy a slow breakfast at the riad. Visit any missed sights — the Majorelle Garden (Jardin Majorelle) is a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent (~150 MAD, book online). The adjacent YSL Museum is excellent if you have interest in fashion and art (~100 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks or the more relaxed boutiques in Gueliz (fixed prices, no bargaining). Pick up argan oil, Moroccan spices (ras el hanout, cumin), leather goods, or handwoven textiles. Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry memories of the Sahara dunes, the ancient medina, mountain valleys, and the warm hospitality of Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — savour the mint tea, msemen, and amlou one last time.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Majorelle Garden at Café Bó Zin or a simple café in Gueliz — croque monsieur, salad, or a light tagine (~120–180 MAD).
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before international flights. Marrakech airport is small but can get congested. Keep 100–200 MAD in cash for tips, last drinks, or small purchases. Declare any argan oil purchases over 1L if flying to the EU. A wonderful trip — Morocco will call you back.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00. Private luxury transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Marrakech Boutique Stay in a chauffeured Mercedes or Range Rover. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your riad suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle introduction to the medina: a private guided walk through the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square to absorb the atmosphere – snake charmers, storytellers, and street musicians. Stroll through the adjacent Souk Semmarine for a sensory first impression without the pressure of deep exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on your riad's rooftop terrace overlooking the medina skyline and the Atlas Mountains. Followed by a welcome dinner at a top Marrakech restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the riad upon arrival – Moroccan mezze, fresh juices, and mint tea
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk (Rue du Souk des Fassis) – refined Moroccan-French cuisine in a beautifully restored 18th-century caravanserai; try the pigeon pastilla and slow-cooked lamb tagine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance through your riad concierge. Request a riad room with Atlas Mountain views. March weather in Marrakech is mild (18–24°C), ideal for rooftop evenings. Tip the driver and porter upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Bahia Palace (9:00 AM) – explore the 19th-century grand vizier's residence with its ornate Moorish tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Follow with a visit to the Saadian Tombs, the lavish 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the El Badi Palace ruins – a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now an evocative open-air site. Visit the adjacent Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues. Conclude with a private tour of the Maison de la Photographie for a visual history of Morocco.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Moroccan hammam experience at a premium spa (e.g., Royal Mansour Spa or Hammam de la Rose) – black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Followed by dinner in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate riad breakfast – msemen (Moroccan flatbread), amlou (argan nut paste), fresh fruit, pastries, and harira soup
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices on Place Rahba Kedima – rooftop terrace with views over the spice market; try the kefta brochettes and Moroccan salad platter
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout – one of Marrakech's legendary palace restaurants; multiple-course Moroccan feast with live Gnawa music, set in a stunning candlelit riad

day_by_day.notes: Book Bahia Palace early morning to beat crowds. The hammam session should be pre-booked. Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Mellah has uneven cobblestones. A private guide (~$80–120 USD) is highly recommended for historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Majorelle Garden (opens 8:00 AM) – the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden co-owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the adjacent Berber Museum housed in Jacques Majorelle's original studio. Arrive early to enjoy it before the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided souk exploration with a personal shopping expert – navigate the labyrinthine souks of the medina: Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk), Souk Cherratine (leatherwork), and Souk Haddadine (metalwork). Enjoy a private leather goods or pottery workshop experience.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop sundowner at Sky Bar (Hôtel & Spa Le Doge) with panoramic medina views. Attend a private Gnawa or Andalusian classical music performance arranged by the riad, followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast – beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), argan honey, fresh orange juice, and Moroccan mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjane) – modern Moroccan cuisine on a stylish rooftop; try the cauliflower chermoula and lamb merguez
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Mamounia's Le Français restaurant – the legendary hotel's brasserie offering refined French-Moroccan fusion in one of the world's most celebrated hotel settings

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden tickets should be booked online in advance. Bargaining is expected in the souks – your shopping guide will help navigate fair prices. Carry small denomination dirhams for souk purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (7:00 AM) in a private luxury 4x4 (Land Cruiser or similar) with a professional driver-guide. Scenic drive through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) – stop for panoramic mountain photography and Berber village visits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Drâa Valley – visit the ancient ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and legendary film location (Game of Thrones, Gladiator, Lawrence of Arabia). Private guided tour of the kasbahs and granaries. Continue driving through the Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs toward Zagora or Merzouga.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge near Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes at sunset. Camel ride into the dunes to watch the sunset paint the Sahara gold and crimson.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast prepared by the riad – croissants, fruit, yogurt, and a thermos of coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant in Ouarzazate – try Restaurant Chez Dimitri (a Ouarzazate institution since 1928) for Moroccan classics and grilled meats
meals.dinner: Candlelit Berber dinner under the stars at the luxury desert camp – traditional mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous, and Moroccan salads; followed by Tuareg drumming and stargazing session

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to the Sahara is approximately 8–10 hours with stops – start early. Bring layers as desert temperatures drop sharply after sunset (March nights can reach 5–8°C). Recommended camps: Scarabeo Camp (Erg Chigaga) or Luxury Erg Chebbi Camp for premium experience with en-suite tented suites.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up (5:30 AM) for a sunrise camel trek or 4x4 dune excursion to the highest dunes. Watch the sun rise over the Sahara – one of Morocco's most transcendent experiences. Optional: hot air balloon flight over the dunes (pre-bookable, weather permitting). Return to camp for a lavish breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sandboarding down the dunes with a guide. Visit a nomadic Berber family encampment for authentic tea ceremony and insight into desert life. Explore a nearby desert oasis and fossil market. Optional quad biking across the erg.
day_by_day.evening: Spa treatment at the desert camp (hammam or massage using argan and desert rose oils). Sunset meditation or yoga on the dunes. Private stargazing session with a telescope guided by a local astronomer – the Sahara offers some of the world's darkest skies.

meals.breakfast: Full camp breakfast after sunrise – eggs, msemen, fresh fruit, coffee, and mint tea served in the open-air dining tent
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the dunes prepared by the camp – Moroccan sandwiches, dates, dried fruits, and fresh mint tea served from traditional teapots
meals.dinner: Gourmet Berber feast at the camp under a canopy of stars – harira soup, bastilla, lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, and traditional Moroccan pastries with orange blossom water

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen and wear a desert scarf (chèche) to protect against sun and sand. Stay hydrated – carry at least 2 liters of water. The hot air balloon must be booked weeks in advance and is subject to wind conditions. March is an excellent month for the Sahara – not too hot (daytime ~25°C).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the desert camp. Final walk in the dunes before checkout. Depart by 9:00 AM in the private 4x4. Stop at the Todra Gorge – a dramatic 300-meter-high canyon carved by the Todra River, ideal for a short hike and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic return journey through the Dadès Valley (Valley of Roses) – in mid-March, the rose bushes may be beginning to bloom. Visit a traditional rose water distillery. Stop at the Skoura Oasis for a walk through its ancient palm grove and ruined kasbahs.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening. Decompress with a private rooftop dinner at the riad or a special restaurant reservation. Reflect on the journey with a nightcap of Moroccan pastilla au lait (milk pastilla dessert) and mint tea.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast – full spread with Moroccan pastries, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Boumalne Dadès – a simple but excellent local restaurant; try the Berber omelette (kefta and egg tagine) and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Farewell Marrakech dinner at Dar Moha – set in a stunning riad with a pool; chef Mohammed Fedal's creative modern Moroccan cuisine is legendary; try the lobster pastilla and lamb with preserved lemon

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is approximately 7–9 hours with stops – pace yourself. The Todra Gorge stop is approximately 1 hour from the desert. Purchase rose water and argan products directly from cooperatives along the route for authentic, fairly priced goods. Confirm dinner reservation before departing the desert.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning – sleep in or enjoy a slow riad breakfast on the courtyard. Visit the Museum of Marrakech (Musée de Marrakech) housed in a stunning 19th-century palace for a curated collection of Moroccan art and artifacts. Explore the nearby Ben Youssef Medersa – a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellige tilework and carved stucco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souk visit for last-minute luxury souvenirs – argan oil, hand-knotted Berber rugs, silver jewelry, or leather babouches. Enjoy a farewell hammam and massage at the riad spa or a nearby luxury spa. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Early farewell dinner before airport transfer (check flight time and adjust accordingly). Private chauffeured transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.

meals.breakfast: Grand final riad breakfast – full spread with all Moroccan staples: harcha, msemen, amlou, honey, fresh fruit, and a pot of spiced Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Le Jardin (Mouassine neighborhood) – a beautiful garden restaurant in a 16th-century riad; try the chicken bastilla and grilled vegetable couscous
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Comptoir Darna – Marrakech's most glamorous restaurant-lounge with belly dancing performances, excellent cocktails, and refined Moroccan-international cuisine; perfect celebratory send-off

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in. Ask the riad concierge to arrange a late checkout if your flight is in the evening. Leave a thank-you tip for riad staff (10–15% of total stay is customary). Carry any liquid argan oil purchases in checked luggage. Dirham cannot be exported – exchange remaining currency before departure.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026
